messages:
clare: Hey folks, got a surprise bill from an ER visit last week. I showed my digital ID but the hospital billed as out-of-network and charged a $450 facility fee. Insurer paid part but balance-billed me. Is there an appeals path or network verification step I missed?

benefits-bot: Quick help: For balance bills try: 1) Confirm provider is in-network via insurer provider lookup; 2) Submit a Balance Billing Dispute or Provider Negotiation request via portal > Claims > Disputes. Link: https://benefits.redwood.com/claims/disputes. Required: EOB, itemized bill, member ID.

Ben: Hi Clare  sorry about that. Two quick questions: did the ER ask for pre-auth (usually not required for emergency care) and which plan are you on (PPO vs EPO)? Emergency services are typically covered in-network even if provider is OON, but billing can get messy.

clare: It was the downtown ER on 3/10. No pre-auth asked. I'm on Redwood Core EPO. The digital ID shows policy code RC-EPO-2026. EOB says "non-participating facility" and insurer allowed $300, leaving $450 billed. I attached the EOB and bill to the portal.

Ben: Thanks. EPOs can be restrictive: if the facility isn't in-network the insurer may only pay emergency allowed amounts. But federal law (EMTALA/No Surprises Act) may protect you from balance billing for emergency services if provider didn't give notice and consent. We should initiate a billing dispute with the carrier and also send a No Surprises Act claim if applicable.

claims-admin: Received the docs. Please confirm whether you received any facility or provider explanation of benefits at the hospital (signed forms) or an "estimate" that you signed. Also, do you have the facility tax ID or NPI on the invoice? That speeds lookup.

clare: I have the itemized invoice with facility NPI 987654321 and a signed consent form for treatment but not a separate estimate. Invoice attached in portal under Claims > Documents.

Ben: Action plan: 1) We'll open a carrier dispute case (we need you to confirm you want Redwood to represent the appeal). 2) We'll submit a No Surprises Act intake to the insurer. 3) If insurer declines, we'll escalate to our broker for independent dispute resolution.

clare: Please go ahead and represent me. I authorize benefits team to share docs with the carrier on my behalf.

claims-admin: On it. Submitted case CASE-NS-20260318-04 to carrier with EOB + invoice. Also filed internal Balance Billing Review (BBR-1782). Carrier ack expected in 3 business days. Note: keep an eye on mail for a provider notice—if they attempted to obtain consent after the fact it can complicate things.

Ben: FYI, if carrier requests patient signature proof or a separate cost estimate we can request the facility to provide an itemized CMS-1500 or UB-04 and a signed Acknowledgement of Emergency Care. I can draft a short release letter to the hospital asking them to waive the balance while dispute is open. Want me to send it?

clare: Yes please, that would be great. I'm worried about the $450 hitting my credit card.

claims-admin: Drafted letter and sending to hospital billing contact now (billing@downtown-er.example). Also asked carrier to suspend collection while dispute is active. I'll post any carrier responses here.

Ben: Quick note: since you're on EPO, future tip is to check insurfer provider lookup before non-emergent visits. For emergency care, always keep itemized bills and EOBs and upload to portal ASAP.

clare: Thank you all  I appreciate the rapid help. Will watch thread for updates. :heart:
